text:
Alice - Support: FYI customer (acme-ml) reports sudden p99 latency spikes when using the new v1.3 model variant with long prompts (~10k tokens). Started ~2026-03-10 14:12 UTC. They see p95 ok but p99 goes to 8-12s from baseline ~1.2s. stack: hosted API, eu-west-1 region.

Alice - Support: sample report attached, paste below. They said it started after we rolled the v1.3-token-splitter change.

Alice - Support: Sample API call (sanitized):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"v1.3-token-split","prompt":"<~10k tokens of user text...>","max_tokens":512}'
```

Alice - Support: Observed metrics from customer: p50 0.9s, p95 1.3s, p99 9.8s. Memory usage on host looks normal. Tokenization_time_ms reported by client side jumps for some requests (10 -> 1200ms).

Priya M (ML): thanks, Alice. I pushed the model onboarding for v1.3 last week. Tokenizer change introduced a new merging pass to handle unicode sequences and some edge-case ligatures — could be expensive on long inputs. Do we have tokenization timing from our infra side?

Ben R - Runtime: I pulled recent runtime traces for that model pool. There are lots of requests showing a large spike during the first N tokens:

```
[runtime-trace] request_id=rc_23a tokenization_ms=14 kv_init_ms=6 encode_ms=1 decode_ms_per_token=1.2 total_ms=1120
[runtime-trace] request_id=rc_24b tokenization_ms=1122 kv_init_ms=5 encode_ms=1 decode_ms_per_token=1.3 total_ms=9800
```

Ben R - Runtime: Looks like tokenization_ms sometimes shoots up to ~1.1s. That matches customer's client-side numbers. Suggest we check whether tokenization moved from C++ -> Python fallback path on certain inputs.

Mateo (SRE): @Ben any correlation with specific hosts/containers? Could be a jittering GC or single-threaded fallback.

Ben R - Runtime: I grep'd logs, the slow tokenizations all hit the new token-merge codepath. There's a guard that calls into python for certain unicode clusters (emoji + ZWJ sequences). If the prompt has a lot of mixed-language text and emoji, it triggers the fallback loop and does quadratic scans.

Priya M (ML): That is plausible. Our local tests used shorter prompts and lacked the emoji-heavy sequences. The new merge pass has O(n*m) behavior on long inputs when many merges occur. Not catastrophic for typical inputs but for 8-12k token prompts it's bad.

Alice - Support: Customer says they don't intentionally send emoji but they do paste PDF-extracted text which has ligatures and weird unicode runs.

Mateo (SRE): Immediate mitigation options we can push now:
- Route acme-ml to a fallback model variant without the new tokenizer (v1.2-stable) via routing policy.
- Add an API-side prefilter to detect long unicode clusters and force legacy-tokenizer path (cheap).
- Add temporary limit for max_input_tokens for this customer (e.g., 4096) and return clear error with guidance.

Priya M (ML): I'll prepare a hotfix to short-circuit the expensive merge pass for inputs > 2048 tokens (fast path: approximate merges). Not ideal long-term but will cut p99. I can ship a model patch today.

Ben R - Runtime: For immediate rollout I recommend: 1) route the customer to v1.2-stable, 2) enable prefix caching on their tenant so repeated prompts share cached KV, 3) set streaming_chunk_size to 64 to reduce single-call tail latency.

Alice - Support: Customer asked for repro steps they can run so we can validate once we push changes. Ben, can you add a minimal repro?

Ben R - Runtime: Repro steps I used locally:
1) create a synthetic prompt by repeating a short unicode run: \"ﬁﬂﬂﬁ\" (ligatures) and alternating with emoji \"👩‍🔬👨‍💻\"  to reach ~9k tokens.
2) POST to /v1/generate with model v1.3-token-split.

Example node snippet: 
```
// reproduce.js (node)
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const p = Array(1200).fill('ﬁﬂ👩‍🔬').join(' ');
fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate',{  
  method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer x','Content-Type':'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'v1.3-token-split', prompt: p, max_tokens: 64})
}).then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log).catch(console.error);
```

Ben R - Runtime: On my laptop that reproduced tokenization_ms 900-1300ms. On v1.2-stable it stays ~15ms.

Mateo (SRE): I'm going to prepare a routing rule and hold a canary: route 100% of acme-ml traffic to v1.2-stable immediately. Will monitor for 10m.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy complete: routing rule applied for tenant=acme-ml -> model=v1.2-stable (change-id: route-3489).

Alice - Support: Customer confirmed ~10m after switch that p99 dropped back to ~1.1s. They still want a proper fix so they can use v1.3 features.

Priya M (ML): I'll push the tokenizer short-circuit patch to the model build: PR #3789. Patch does: detect long input lengths, skip expensive unicode-merge pass and fall back to byte-level merges (significantly faster). Shipping as v1.3.1. Also adding regression tests with 10k token synthetic sequences and PDF-extracted text corpus.

Ben R - Runtime: Once PR is merged, we should run a canary on a non-production pool, then enable v1.3.1 for 10% traffic, run perf job that exercises 10k token prompts and emoji mixes. I'll add an alert: tokenization_ms > 300ms for >1% of requests -> pager.

Priya M (ML): PR merged and build started. Build tag: v1.3.1-rc1.

deploy-bot: build succeeded: v1.3.1-rc1. deploy plan ready.

Mateo (SRE): Running perf canary: routing 5% traffic to v1.3.1-rc1 in eu-west-1 pool. Monitoring tokenization_ms histogram.

Ben R - Runtime: Early numbers look good: tokenization p99 ~85ms on synthetic corpora. No significant CPU or memory regression.

Priya M (ML): Merging canary -> stable, will tag v1.3.1. I also opened follow-ups: optimize merge algorithm (O(n) approach) and add fuzz tests for unicode clusters.

deploy-bot: deployment completed: v1.3.1 promoted to stable in eu-west-1 (deploy-id: dpl-5566).

Alice - Support: Customer confirmation: they saw p99 back to 1.2s; reported no functional regressions. They're happy to try v1.3.1 for a week and we can monitor.

Mateo (SRE): Postmortem notes action items:
- [P0] Add automatic detection for heavy unicode clusters and route tokenizer fallback early.
- [P1] Add regression test suite with PDF-extracted and emoji-heavy samples.
- [P1] Improve observability: expose tokenization_ms per-request in admin dashboard.
- [P2] Research full O(n) merge algorithm and land in tokenizer lib.

Priya M (ML): I'll schedule work for P1/P2 and link PRs in the ticket.

Ben R - Runtime: For customers: we can add a temporary tenant-level preference `tokenizer=legacy|v1.3` to let support route without needing full deploy. Ops-safety net.

Alice - Support: Thanks all. I'll close the immediate escalation and keep the customer updated weekly.

Alice - Support: Marking thread resolved for now. If we see new regressions, reopen. :white_check_mark:
